_doc: chainId and NAMES that 9Chain-A1 has DELIBERATELY released back into circulation. This file is the ONLY thing that lets `chainid-issued.json` shrink: `gen-chainid-issued.mjs --write` refuses any loss not accounted for here, so a source ledger going missing can never quietly hand a name back. Written and reviewed by a human, never generated.
_why_a_file_and_not_a_flag: A shrinking block-list is the exact failure the block-list exists to prevent, so the authority to shrink it must live somewhere a reviewer can read months later. A command-line flag leaves no trace; this file names every entry that was let go, who decided, and why.

releases.reason: Every chainId and name below was created by the A1 team’s own testing (Smoke*, CauDich*, CauNguon*, Warp*, Tai*, Pkhongphi*, Pthongluo*, Ptuintien*, Pchichude*, Pkin*, ViThu*, BuocTest*, GiaoDienTest, OwnerTest, DeltaChain, OmegaChain, Eric1/eric1, David Do). None was ever handed to an outside user, so there is no promise to keep. g1 opens with a clean name space.
releases.safe_because: chainId REPLAY is prevented by architecture, not by this list: generation g issues only inside [9000000000 + g*1000000, +999999], so g1 issues 9001000000-9001999999 and can never re-emit 9100-9145, 9201 or 9000000010/11 whatever this file says. Releasing therefore affects the NAME half only, and no released name was ever held outside the team.
releases.note: `eric1` does not appear under names: the ledger folds names case-insensitively, so it is carried by `Eric1`. Releasing `Eric1` releases both.
